articles.title: Cheltenham’s long awaited return proves romance lives on in jumps racing
articles.summary: Outsider wins Sharp Novices’ Hurdle at 20-1. Trainer John Dawson gets better of Dan Skelton. The jumping game increasingly resembles the Flat when it comes to the concentration of racing power in ever fewer trainers’ hands, but the opening day of Cheltenham’s new season – the first, in fact, since…
body: Dan Skelton, who dethroned Willie Mullins to become the new champion over jumps last season, had already trained 115 winners in the current campaign before racing on Friday, nearly halfway towards Martin Pipe’s all-time record of 243. John Dawson, by contrast, had sent out a total of six winners from his yard in North Yorkshire since May 2023.

However, it was Dawson’s Kingofthefrontier, a 20-1 outsider and only the trainer’s third runner at the home of jumping, who led the field home in the Grade Two Sharp Novices’ Hurdle, with Skelton’s Cooltobecareless, the 13-8 favourite, only third. The winner was nearer last than first turning in but showed an impressive turn of foot to run out a two-and-a-quarter length winner from Nicky Henderson’s Planters Punch.

Dawson rode into the famous winner’s enclosure aboard Sine Nomine after the Hunters’ Chase at the festival meeting here in March 2024, but his first Cheltenham winner as a trainer was an even better moment in what is still a young racing career.
“We’ve always loved him since the word go,” Dawson said. “I just felt we had a horse to come and have a go with.

articles.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
articles.summary: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status. Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists. Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal.
body: The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries.

The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability.

The NWSLPA opposed the mechanism and filed a grievance, arguing that the classification of players was a violation of federal labor law and the existing collective bargaining agreement. About 100 players had qualified for the designation based on the criteria – a total that, at the time the rule was introduced, included the likes of Trinity Rodman and Sophia Wilson but would have excluded such players as two-time NWSL MVP Sam Kerr and US star Catarina Macario.

articles.title: ‘A different kid’: from karting to F1 champion-elect, Antonelli’s ability has always stood out
articles.summary: With first drivers’ title all but secure, a friendlier champion would be hard to find, but Italian’s eight wins this season speak to his focus. Even as Kimi Antonelli may be world champion-elect, it is sometimes hard to equate the young man who has driven with such exceptional skill and no little…
body: Whether the Italian seals his place as F1’s youngest world champion, at 20 years old, at this Sunday’s US Grand Prix in Austin or the next round in Mexico or even beyond that is moot – that he will do so is all but assured and for all that he is still in only his second season in the sport, a more rounded, well-liked champion than the Mercedes driver would be hard to find.

Engage with Antonelli and it is almost impossible not to still see the three-year-old child who insisted on taking to his father Marco’s knee to try out the racing simulator the former driver had brought home. Marco would control the pedals and his son the wheel with an irrepressible enthusiasm that could barely be contained and is still there in every dart, feint and incisive pass he makes today.

articles.title: AFC Wimbledon's Skiverton diagnosed with cancer
articles.summary: AFC Wimbledon assistant manager Terry Skiverton is scheduled to begin treatment in the coming weeks after being diagnosed with throat cancer.
body: AFC Wimbledon assistant manager Terry Skiverton has been diagnosed with throat cancer and is scheduled to begin treatment in the coming weeks.
The League One club said Skiverton had faced further health challenges since announcing in July that he would take time away from his duties to recover from ankle surgery.

A club statement said:, external "Terry has been receiving valuable support from the League Managers Association (LMA) in recent months, and the club will continue to stand alongside him and his family throughout his treatment and recovery.
"Everyone at AFC Wimbledon sends Terry their heartfelt best wishes as he prepares for the next stage of his treatment."

"Now I'm back drinking and recovering. Now I'm going to start eating. Eat food first, then tomorrow you guys already know who I'm going to eat."

articles.title: Rick Pitino calls out NCAA's handling of eligibility lawsuits, decision to ask Congress for help
articles.summary: With less than two weeks to go until the college basketball season starts, there’s still uncertainty around eligibility amid multiple lawsuits. St. John’s coach Rick Pitino has questions, but mostly about how the NCAA handled the rule changes and the legal challenges.
body: Pitino told Jon Rothstein he sees comments from other coaches who aren’t happy with the NCAA, given the state of the landscape. However, his counter is that the schools are part of the association, though he acknowledged “mistakes” with regard to eligibility.

To Pitino, the NCAA had an opportunity to draw a line – particularly when it comes to professional athletes – and didn’t. As a result, he wondered why the governing body continues to fight the lawsuits while also lobbying for the Protect College Sports Act in Congress.

“A lot of coaches have been upset at the NCAA and then knocking the NCAA,” Pitino said on CBS Sports’ Inside College Basketball Now. “Look, what you have to understand is we are the NCAA. We’re part of this corporation. The NCAA just made some mistakes because they’re caught with all this at the last second. Now, if the NCAA said on Nov. 15, ‘We’re going to allow for this class to play a fifth year,’ there would be none of this.

articles.title: Frauen-Bundesliga: Bayern’s five-star display extends unbeaten run as Leipzig fall apart
articles.summary: Bayern Munich made light work of RB Leipzig to claim a 5–1 away victory in the Frauen-Bundesliga, with Klara Bühl scoring twice in a commanding performance that extended the defending champions’...
body: Momoko Tanikawa opened the scoring inside eight minutes before Zenia Mertens’ own goal doubled Bayern’s advantage six minutes later. Bühl struck twice after the break, and Edna Imade added a fifth to cap another convincing afternoon for José Barcala’s side. Marleen Schimmer briefly offered Leipzig a response, but the hosts could not turn that moment into a comeback.
The result was more than another three points for Bayern. It was a reminder of how quickly their quality can turn a competitive fixture into a one-sided contest.

Bayern wasted little time establishing control. Tanikawa’s eighth-minute goal gave the visitors an early foothold, and Leipzig’s afternoon deteriorated further when Mertens inadvertently put the ball into her own net in the 14th minute.

Two goals behind inside the opening quarter-hour, Leipzig faced the difficult task of chasing a side comfortable in possession and dangerous whenever space opened up. Bayern finished with 67 per cent of the ball, 16 shots and nine efforts on target, compared with Leipzig’s four shots on target from 13 attempts.

articles.title: What Dalton Knecht Offers Knicks As A Two-Way Signing
articles.summary: After the New York Knicks lost their season opener, they are already bringing in reinforcements. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, the team has signed former Los Angeles Lakers forward Dalton Knecht to a two-way contract.
body: Signing Knecht in favor of McCullar is an improvement on the depth options the Knicks have. Though both are in their third seasons in the league, Knecht has much more NBA experience than McCullar. Knecht has appeared in 132 regular season games compared to McCullar’s 25. Jaden Akins and Tyler Nickel, the Knicks’ other two players on two-way contracts, are rookies. Neither was active for the opener on Tuesday, but McCullar was active and received his championship ring with the rest of the squad.

Now, Knecht will be a much likelier option to receive playing time as a wing when in need for offense than the likes of the two rookies. Akins and Nickel are currently with the G League affiliate Westchester Knicks, where Knecht will likely spend some time playing as well if the team doesn’t feel that he’s needed for injury relief.

Knecht was waived before the Lakers’ opener, debuting the new big three, as he’d failed to earn preseason playing time. He also apparently stagnated in his sophomore season in 2025-26. Knetch was sent to the G League ‘s South Bay Lakers last December.

articles.summary: appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Seattle Seahawks will be facing the Kansas City Chiefs this week in hopes of getting back on track after losing their last two games.
body: It’s uncertain how much time he could see on the field, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Network believes that it can be a lot.

“I would expect him to play; I don’t know the carry load yet. He’s back full go. They really have taken their time. They’ve used the full three weeks, so I would expect him to play and to play a lot,” Rapoport said on the Pat McAfee Show.

That’s good news for the Seahawks, as Charbonnet is the best back they have on the roster as of now. Since he’s been injured this season, they’ve been going with a committee at the position, and though there were flashes, the consistency just hasn’t been there.
The hope is that Charbonnet can give them the boost that they need, and that can even open up things for Sam Darnold in the passing game.

articles.title: Leclerc tops first USA practice as upgraded Ferrari shows early promise
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc showed early promise in an upgraded Ferrari car to pip Red Bull's in-form Max Verstappen to the fastest time of first practice at the United States Grand Prix.
body: Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull all introduced fresh revisions to their cars for the opening hour of running at the Circuit of the Americas, which is staging the first leg of the sport's second of three end-of-season triple headers.

Ferrari's package features changes to their car's floor, sidepod and diffuser and showed speed on both the medium and soft tyres around the undulating COTA lap, with Leclerc ultimately setting the session's pace on the latter with a best lap of 1:36.052.

Verstappen, the winner of the last two races, finished 0.084s behind Leclerc although lost a quicker lap on the softs which was two tenths faster than the Ferrari due to a track limits violation at Turn 19.

Lando Norris was third in a McLaren car which also features changes as they bid to return to form after a difficult run of races saw them slip into the clutches of Red Bull in the Constructors' Championship battle for third.

articles.title: Cordina: I've been offered Pacquiao fight on AJ-Fury card
articles.summary: Welsh boxer Joe Cordina has told Sky Sports that he has been offered a fight with Manny Pacquiao as part of the undercard for the blockbuster all-British heavyweight clash between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury on December.
body: The 34-year-old has confirmed that he has agreed to fight the boxing icon at the Principality Stadium in his birth city of Cardiff, but that no contracts have been signed as of yet.

"I've been offered the fight," said Cordina, a two-time super-featherweight world champion. "They asked me if I'd fight Pacquiao: this is what the deal is, otherwise they're going to offer it to someone else.

"'Of course', I said, 'No problem'. I've won world titles, and don't get me wrong, I want to win more. But, for me, the name of Manny Pacquiao at this present moment is bigger than any name in boxing.
"He's an eight-division world champion, a legend. But a global superstar like him will be gone in the next year or so.

articles.title: Jesse Legree, nation's leading receiver, announces return to Oregon State for sophomore year
articles.summary: A midseason All-American with 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns, the breakout freshman delivers a massive statement for the Beavers by bypassing the transfer portal
body: Jesse Legree – the nation's most exciting freshman and a midseason CBS Sports All-America selection – announced to the world Friday from his home gym in Baltimore, Maryland, that he will be returning to Oregon State for his sophomore season. Legree made the announcement and re-signed with the Beavers live on CBS Sports HQ.

Legree's intent during the bye week was to put to rest doubts about his future and quiet portal whispers that had already begun as scouting departments around the country, beginning to devise their 2027 roster-building plans, took full notice of the 5-foot-9 Legree's exploits in Corvallis: 46 receptions and a nation-leading 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns.

"I, here, will be signing to Oregon State Beavers for the 2027 to 2028 season," Legree said. "It's always some kids' dream to live out on signing day, and unfortunately, I wasn't able to have mine last year. And to be able to have one this year for this contract is great."
